note: Patches applied to a pinned sibling checkout before generation, so a module the compiler refuses to lower today can still ship. A patch here may only rewrite an expression into an equivalent the compiler does lower. It may NEVER change observable behavior -- absence, reference identity, equality, ordering, exception shape, task settlement -- because the generated header is then tested against the patched source, so a behavioral patch is a lie our own tests would certify. Each patch states the equivalence that makes it safe and the refusal it answers. The patch is applied after the pin integrity check and reverted when generation ends, so the checkout is only ever dirty inside one run. `baseCommit` pins the patch to the revision it was written against: a pin move that breaks the patch fails loudly instead of silently applying to different code.

patches.refusal: `x ??= y` whose target has a declared type with no absent member is emitted as the target alone, so the write disappears. An `unknown`/`any` target is carried as the erased `flight::Any`, whose nullishness is a runtime property of the value rather than of the type, so the no-op shortcut is unsound for exactly that carrier: `failure ??= error;` in a catch body emits a bare `failure;`, the first failure is never recorded, and the `if (failure !== null) throw failure;` that follows can never fire -- a failed teardown becomes indistinguishable from a successful one. Measured in `@flighthq/power`'s `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower`; the same construct first appears in `particleEmitterSignals.ts`, whose record-typed target took a different lowering lane and so did not show it.
patches.rewrite: One branch of the assignment lowering: a `??=` target whose declared type has no absent member AND whose C++ carrier is the erased `flight::Any` (IR type kind `unknown`) now lowers to the guarded assignment `([&]() { auto&& assignment_target = LEFT; if (assignment_target.is_nullish()) assignment_target = RIGHT; return assignment_target; }())`, using the carrier's own loose nullish test. A target whose carrier cannot hold a nullish value -- a `number` target's `double` -- keeps the no-op, and a target carried as an optional keeps `emitLogicalAssignmentCpp`. Catch breadth is deliberately untouched: the handler remains `catch (const std::exception&)`, which is a separate open defect (docs/compiler-requests/catch-handler-breadth-attempt-all.md).
patches.equivalence: The old shortcut returned the target unmodified, which is the correct lowering only where the carrier cannot hold null or undefined; that is now the only case that keeps it. Where the carrier is the erased `flight::Any`, the emitted code records the right-hand side exactly when JavaScript would, and the loose `is_nullish()` matches `??=`'s rule that null and undefined both assign rather than either strict half. An assignment still evaluates to the target's value, the condition is evaluated once per evaluation, a target that already holds a value is left alone -- which is what retains the FIRST failure across later iterations -- and no absent member, no refusal, and no runtime capability is invented.
patches.verification: New `cppNullishAssignmentStatement.test.ts`, 4 pass: the `??=` statement inside a catch body keeps a conditional write and is no longer a bare target; the same holds in an expression position; the guard is the loose `is_nullish()`, not either strict half; and a number target keeps the no-op. Reverting the branch fails 3 of those 4 and leaves the number-target case passing. `cppCompilerBackend.test.ts` reports the same 24 failures before and after the change (pre-existing at this base, none of them this shape), so the branch adds no regression and removes none. The companion patch compiler-catch-recorded-slot-carrier claims the catch-recorded slot, so this test's fixtures were retargeted to shapes it does not claim; the pair was re-verified together: all 40 compiler patches apply in manifest order over a clean checkout and both backend test files pass 9/9.
patches.unblocks: `@flighthq/power`'s attempt-all teardown: `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower` promise in their own source comment to rethrow the first failure once the siblings have run, which their emitted bodies could not do. Regenerating the package's slice with this patch is what the unit's second half measures; the behaviour left unasserted there is the catch-breadth half, which stays open.
patches.expires: when the emitter distinguishes a carrier that cannot hold a nullish value from one whose value decides it without the declared-absence-member test.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The defect is one condition in the pinned backend's assignment lowering that mis-classifies an erased carrier, not a missing contract, so it needs no new runtime capability and no new evidence channel -- the carrier's own `is_nullish()` already exists and is already used elsewhere in the same file. A narrow versioned patch repairs the pinned implementation, and the focused backend test it carries is the regression guard for the exact shape.

patches.refusal: an `unknown` slot that a catch/attempt-all pattern records into is carried as `std::exception_ptr` only when it has NO initializer, records with `=` and is read nowhere but its record and its rethrow. `let failure: unknown = null;` therefore stays on the erased `flight::Any` path, which cannot hold a caught exception at all: with the record lowering in place the emitted assignment does not compile. The same source shape without the initializer lowers correctly, so the initializer alone decides whether the caught value is representable.
patches.rewrite: Three conditions in the exception-slot election and two lanes that must agree with it. The candidate now admits an initializer that is a nullish literal (`null`/`undefined`, which is the same 'no failure recorded yet' an empty `std::exception_ptr` means), a `??=` whose right side is a catch binding counts as a recording assignment rather than an invalid one, and a nullish presence test of the slot counts as a permitted reference. The record lane lowers `slot ??= caught` to `if (!slot) slot = std::current_exception();`, which keeps the FIRST failure, and the presence-test lane lowers the slot's nullish test to pointer emptiness for either sentinel. Everything else stays: a slot initialized to a non-nullish value, recorded from anything but a catch binding, never rethrown, or read for its value rather than its presence keeps the erased carrier.
patches.equivalence: An empty `std::exception_ptr` and the source's `null` initializer are the same state -- 'nothing recorded yet' -- so admitting the initializer changes which carrier is chosen, not what the program means; the `??=` guard assigns exactly when the slot is empty, which is `??=`'s rule for this carrier and is what retains the first failure; and both sentinels answer the same way because the slot only ever holds either nothing or a recorded exception. Reference counting still requires every read of the slot to be a record, the rethrow, or the presence test, so a slot whose *value* other code consumes is untouched, and the catch handler itself is not changed in any way: it stays `catch (const std::exception&)`, so non-class throws still escape a continuing handler, which remains the separate open defect.
patches.verification: New `cppCatchRecordedSlotCarrier.test.ts`, 5 pass: the attempt-all slot takes `std::exception_ptr`, records once through the guarded `current_exception()`, is tested as pointer emptiness rather than through the erased carrier, and rethrows through `std::rethrow_exception`; and three controls keep `flight::Any` -- an ordinary `unknown` slot assigned a plain value, a slot recorded but never rethrown, and a slot read for its value as well as its presence. Running the same file against the record-lowering patch alone fails 2 of those 5 (the carrier and the presence test) and passes the three controls. `cppCompilerBackend.test.ts` reports the same 24 failures with both patches as it does with the record patch alone and with neither (pre-existing at this base). It also retargets the fixtures of compiler-nullish-assignment-statement-in-catch, whose own fixture is a catch-recorded slot this patch now claims; verified together by applying all 40 compiler patches in manifest order to a clean checkout (0 failures) and running both backend test files there, 9/9.
patches.unblocks: Regenerating `@flighthq/power` package-scoped with both patches: `destroyPowerKeepAwake` and `detachPower` compile, record the first failure of an attempt-all teardown, and rethrow it -- the behaviour their source comments promise. With the record patch alone the module does not compile at all, so the two patches are a pair.
patches.expires: when the election asks what the slot's carrier must be able to hold rather than how the source happened to spell its initializer, record, and reads.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The election is a closed-shape rule in the pinned backend with its own stated intent in a comment -- it protects ordinary unknown storage from the exception carrier -- and these three conditions are that intent spelled more precisely, not a new contract: the carrier, the record and the rethrow it needs all already exist. A narrow versioned patch with focused controls is the smallest change that lets the source's own attempt-all shape lower, and the controls are what keep the rule from widening.

patches.refusal: a `catch (error)` whose body only reifies the caught value -- the attempt-all teardown that records the first failure and rethrows it after the siblings -- is emitted as `catch (const std::exception& error)`. A thrown value that is not a class therefore never reaches the handler: it escapes, the loop is skipped, and the remaining obligations are stranded. C++ has a value channel for this (`throw 42`), and `std::current_exception()` reifies any thrown value, so the narrow binding is not a representation limit -- it is a binding the body does not need.
patches.rewrite: In the catch-clause emission, a handler whose binding is referenced ONLY as the right side of a record into a slot carried as `std::exception_ptr` -- the record the exception-carrier patch lowers to `std::current_exception()`, which never mentions the binding -- is emitted as `catch (...)`. A handler that reads the value (a member, an argument, a direct rethrow) keeps `catch (const std::exception& name)`, because C++ cannot name a non-class caught value at all; that is the boundary this lowering stops at, and staying narrow there is deliberate. A handler with no binding is unchanged (`catch (...)` already).
patches.equivalence: The value rethrown is the value caught, for every thrown type: `std::rethrow_exception` rethrows the same object a class throw produced -- a caller catching `flight::Error` sees exactly what it saw before -- and rethrows the same `int` a primitive throw produced, which the narrow handler could not deliver at all. The record is still `std::current_exception()` and the rethrow is still `std::rethrow_exception`, so first-failure retention is unchanged, and the attempt-all loop now runs its siblings for a non-class throw instead of being skipped by it. Nothing is boxed into a carrier it was not: the widening is exactly 'catch everything, keep the exception pointer', and where that is not faithful the handler is left narrow.
patches.verification: New `cppCatchHandlerBreadth.test.ts`, 4 pass: the reify-only attempt-all handler is `catch (...)` with the exception-pointer record and rethrow; a handler that rethrows the binding directly and one that records it into a NON-exception slot both keep the narrow `catch (const std::exception& error)`; and a binding-less handler is unchanged. Neutralising the condition fails the first case and leaves the three boundary controls passing. Applied with the other compiler patches in manifest order, all 41 apply and the three backend test files pass 13/13; the behavioural proof for a primitive throw is in `@flighthq/power`'s native test.
patches.unblocks: `@flighthq/power`'s attempt-all teardown is faithful for every thrown value it can be given: with a provider whose destroy throws a number, the sibling is still attempted and the caller catches that same number, where the narrow handler skipped the sibling and the value escaped.
patches.expires: when the emitter can name a non-class caught value where the source reads it, at which point the narrow form is never needed.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The narrow form is a binding choice in the catch-clause emission, not a missing contract: the value channel (`catch (...)`, `std::current_exception()`, `std::rethrow_exception`) is already used elsewhere in the same file and already lowered for the binding-less handler. The patch narrows exactly which handlers may keep the binding, and its controls pin the boundary.

patches.refusal: `x instanceof T` reaches the C++ as the source operator. C++ has no `instanceof`, so a translation unit that reaches one stops at the parse: the emitted header is neither the source answer nor a refusal, and no ledger records it because nothing was refused. Measured on the property read `response.body` of `NetResponseBody` in @flighthq/audio's audioResourceFrom.ts line 102 and @flighthq/loader's load.ts line 51, each failing `expected ')'` at the guard.
patches.rewrite: Lowers the test onto the operand's carrier through ONE runtime question, `flight::union_kind_if`, and routes the projection the guard proves through its throwing twin `flight::union_kind_or_throw`. The question is a compile-time walk of the carrier (optional, variant, or a bare erased value): an alternative of the target's own type answers with a pointer into the carrier, an `Any` alternative is asked through its checked external view, and anything else -- a string, an absence, an `Any` holding another type -- answers null without throwing. An operand with no recorded type, a union that neither names the target nor carries the erased arm, a target naming a source class or an unbound ambient, and a reference-shaped target (which has no stable view out of the erased carrier) each refuse by rule.
patches.equivalence: The guard and the projection ask the same question of the same carrier, so the guard can never admit a value the projection cannot produce -- which is what makes a projection without the proof behind it the only way the throwing twin can fire, and that is a compiler defect rather than a source-observable failure (`std::logic_error`, never a `flight::Error` a source `catch` could take for an application failure). The answer is a pointer INTO the carrier: the object that was there, never a copy, so reference identity survives. Answering false without throwing for a string, an absence, or an `Any` holding another type is the source's own answer for a value its guard rejected. Where the union has no erased arm the projection stays on the slot the source's alternative holds, so no package's emitted code moves for a union that could not reach one.

patches.refusal: A guarded read whose declared union the analysis cannot state has no proof to project through, even though the guard that dominates it names the alternative AND the carrier it tested. Measured on @flighthq/audio's audioResourceFrom.ts and @flighthq/loader's load.ts, whose `response.body` is declared through an alias (`body: NetResponseBody`): the analysis states the name rather than the union, the emitter expands the name when it chooses the carrier, and the read is left handing the whole carrier to a constructor that takes one alternative -- a conversion the target refuses.
patches.rewrite: The backend carries what its own lowering already proved. A lowered `instanceof` guard records, for the branch it controls, the alternative it named for the path it tested -- the emitted `flight::union_kind_if` names both -- and a read of that same path inside the branch is emitted as that question's throwing twin, from the SAME carrier expansion. No alias is resolved a second time and no type reference is materialized that the module never wrote. The proof's lifetime is TypeScript's: a write to the path or to any prefix withdraws it before the statement that writes it is even emitted (an assignment target is a write, not a read, and a projection onto an lvalue is not C++); a call withdraws it for the statements AFTER it, because a property narrowing is invalidated at any call while a read inside the call's own statement is evaluated before it runs; and it never leaves the branch that proves it. A read the semantic layer's own proof already reaches is left to that proof, so nothing is projected twice.
patches.equivalence: The read is emitted from the guard's own proof, so the two cannot disagree: the projection is the throwing twin of the test that admitted the branch, over the same carrier expression. Its answer is a reference INTO that carrier, so the value is the one that was there and not a copy, and a divergence -- a projection emitted where the guard did not hold -- is a std::logic_error rather than a value the source could have observed. The lifetime rules are the ones the source language already has for a property narrowing, and each of them is a withdrawal rather than an invention: where the proof is gone the read is emitted exactly as it was before this patch.

The binding keeps its representation, its name, and its downstream rules; only its lifetime crosses the suspension. A handler whose carrier is re-bound keeps the NARROW `catch (const std::exception&)`, because a thrown value that is not a class exception has no such representation to re-bind -- which the source's own narrowing never admits either. The pass accepts the re-binding read as the one read of the carrier, so a slot read by anything else is still ordinary storage.
patches.equivalence: The object is the one that was thrown, not a copy: `std::current_exception()` owns the exception object, and `flight::caught_exception` rethrows that pointer and returns the object it delivers, so a hoisted body reads exactly what its handler caught -- the same address, the same subclass, through the same `static_cast<flight::Error>`/`Any` conversions every non-awaiting catch already uses. A rejection built from the carrier settles with that same object. Its failure mode is a `std::logic_error` for a carrier read where nothing was caught, which no source program can reach and no source `catch` can take for an application error. A body that never reads its binding, and every catch that never awaits, emit exactly as before.

patches.refusal: A callable that accepts FEWER parameters than the callable it is stored into was stored as itself. TypeScript passes the extra arguments and the source ignores them; `std::function` requires one exact signature and refuses the narrower one. Measured on @flighthq/loader's resourceLoader.ts, where `_noopLoad` (one parameter) is stored into `PendingEntry.wrappedLoad` (two) -- the first compile error in that module once it stopped being a placeholder, and not the module's remaining refusal.
patches.rewrite: The position's own callable is what the source is adapted TO, and that adaptation already exists in this file for a callable slot inside a union; what was missing was a plain callable position reaching it. A new entry point resolves the position's declared callable -- through an alias, and deliberately NOT through a union or optional carrier, which has its own path that wraps the adapted callable -- and, where the source's parameter list differs from it, emits that same wrapper. A source REQUIRING more parameters than the target promises is refused rather than wrapped, because it would be called with fewer arguments than it declares. The wrapper also now collects the arguments a rest-parameter source accepts into the array the source language would have built for it.
patches.equivalence: The wrapper is the source's own call, with the parameters the source does not accept left out or supplied absence: a declaration is invoked directly (a stateless function address), and any other callable is evaluated ONCE where the callable is created and retained by value, so the callable the target holds is the one the source produced -- a copied `std::function` shares its own state -- and no produced expression is re-run per invocation. The arguments the source does receive are the first ones, in order, converted exactly as the position already converts them; a source-only optional parameter is supplied `std::nullopt` so its default applies; a rest parameter receives every remaining argument in one array; and the wrapper returns the source's result, so the return domain is the declared one and an exception the source raises propagates unchanged. An equal signature is left alone, and a source with more declared parameters whose extras are optional is adapted rather than refused.

Every value WITHOUT U+0000 takes the branch that emits byte-identical text to before, so no other header changes, including the eight committed ones that carry a literal of their own. Nothing else about the constructor changes: `String(std::string_view)` is the overload `String(const char*)` already delegated to, so the UTF-8 decoding, the empty-string result for an empty literal, and value identity are the same.

patches.rewrite: In `new` expression emission, a flight-cpp `new Map(argument)` whose single argument is itself a Map or ReadonlyMap is spelled `flight::Map<K, V>(argument).clone()`. Map::clone() copies every record in insertion order into new storage. Every other Map constructor form (entry arrays, iterators, literals, empty) is emitted exactly as before.
patches.equivalence: `new Map(map)` creates a new Map holding map's entries in map's iteration order; clone() of the constructed Map is exactly that. When the argument already has the constructed type, the constructor shares and clone() copies; when it has another element type, the range constructor has already copied and clone() copies the fresh map again, which is redundant and unobservable. The source map is never written, and Map's live iteration over its own storage is unchanged.
